q: Sheffield United beat Manchester United 2–1 at Bramall Lane on 15 August 1992, in a game that produced the very first goal of the Premier League era. Which Blades player scored it?
hint: Deane scored twice that afternoon, one of them from the penalty spot, and his opener was the first goal the new competition ever saw.

q: On the opening day of the first Premier League season in August 1992, Sheffield United won 2–1 at Bramall Lane against which club?
hint: The visitors went on to win that inaugural Premier League title, but they lost their opening fixture in Sheffield in front of 28,070.

q: Sheffield United contest the Steel City derby with which club?
hint: The two Sheffield clubs sit a few miles apart — Wednesday at Hillsborough, United at Bramall Lane.

q: Chris Wilder's first season in charge, 2016–17, ended with Sheffield United winning the League One title. How many points did they finish on?
hint: Wilder, a boyhood Blade, ended a six-season stay in the third tier at the first attempt — and the Blades reached three figures.

q: Sheffield United were relegated from the Premier League on the final day of the 2006–07 season. Who was their manager?
hint: He had taken the club up as Championship runners-up the season before, and left within days of the relegation-day defeat at Bramall Lane.

q: Who was Sheffield United's leading scorer in the 2018–19 Championship season, with 23 league goals, as the club won promotion to the Premier League?
hint: The Sheffield-born striker came through the club's own academy; McGoldrick was next on the list that season with 15.

q: Sheffield United were relegated from the Premier League on the final day of 1993–94, losing 3–2 away to which club?
hint: Mark Stein scored twice at Stamford Bridge on 7 May 1994, the second in stoppage time, on a chaotic final afternoon that sent the Blades down in 20th.

q: Sheffield United lost the 1993 FA Cup semi-final 2–1 to Sheffield Wednesday. At which ground was the all-Sheffield tie played?
hint: Chris Waddle's second-minute free-kick and Mark Bright's extra-time header settled it; Alan Cork had equalised for United.

q: In 2002–03 Sheffield United reached both domestic cup semi-finals. Which club knocked them out of the League Cup?
hint: United won the first leg 2–1 at Bramall Lane, but lost 2–0 after extra time at Anfield to go out 3–2 on aggregate — and the winners lifted the trophy.

q: Sheffield United lost the 2003 First Division play-off final 3–0 at the Millennium Stadium. Which club beat them?
hint: Dave Jones's side led 3–0 by half-time in Cardiff through Mark Kennedy, Nathan Blake and Kenny Miller; United had beaten Nottingham Forest 5–4 on aggregate in the semi-final.

q: Sheffield United went up to the Premier League as Championship runners-up in 2005–06. Which club won the title that season with 106 points?
hint: The champions ran away with it on 106 points while the Blades finished second on 90; Watford came up through the play-offs.

q: On the final day of 2006–07 Sheffield United were relegated after losing 2–1 at Bramall Lane. Who were the visitors that afternoon?
hint: Both clubs finished on 38 points and the visitors survived on goal difference; Jon Stead had equalised before a first-half penalty won it.

q: In a 1–0 home win in December 2006, Phil Jagielka spent the last half-hour in goal after Paddy Kenny was injured. Which club were Sheffield United beating?
hint: Jagielka, an outfield player, kept the clean sheet and made a save from Robin van Persie to seal one of the Blades' best results of that Premier League season.

q: Sheffield United were promoted to the Premier League as Championship runners-up in 2018–19. Which club finished above them as champions?
hint: The champions took 94 points; the Blades finished on 89, six clear of Leeds United, and Aston Villa came up through the play-offs.

q: Sheffield United's first-choice goalkeeper during their ninth-place 2019–20 Premier League season was on loan from which club?
hint: Dean Henderson played 36 league games on loan as Chris Wilder's newly promoted side, tipped by most pundits for relegation, finished ninth.

q: Who was Sheffield United's top scorer in 2002–03, with 16 league goals?
hint: He was a central midfielder rather than a forward, and finished with 22 in all competitions in the season United reached two cup semi-finals and the play-off final.

q: Arsenal beat Sheffield United 1–0 in the 2003 FA Cup semi-final. At which ground was the tie played?
hint: Freddie Ljungberg scored in the 34th minute in front of 59,170 and David Seaman produced a famous late save; Arsenal went on to win the cup.

q: Which Sheffield United midfielder scored both goals in the 2–1 League Cup semi-final first-leg win over Liverpool in January 2003?
hint: The homegrown midfielder struck in the 76th and 82nd minutes at Bramall Lane, but Liverpool overturned the tie at Anfield.

q: Who scored the penalty for Wigan Athletic that relegated Sheffield United on the final day of the 2006–07 season?
hint: The defender had left Bramall Lane for Wigan that January; his first-half penalty, awarded for a Phil Jagielka handball, kept Wigan up on goal difference.

q: In June 2020, Sheffield United were denied a clear goal when goal-line technology failed to register that the ball had crossed the line. The 0–0 draw was away at which club?
hint: Hawk-Eye apologised unreservedly, saying its cameras were blocked by the goalkeeper, a defender and the post as Ørjan Nyland carried Oliver Norwood's free-kick over his own line.
